plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. This is because your payment depends on the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so bidding your value ensures you win whenever profitable (value exceeds the second-highest bid) and never overpay. Bidding below value risks losing profitable auctions; bidding above value risks losses. With no prior history to adjust for, truthful bidding maximizes expected profit.

In a second-price auction (winner pays second-highest bid), bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of opponents' strategies. This is because if I bid below my value, I risk losing auctions I could have profitably won; if I bid above my value, I risk winning at a price higher than my value, causing a loss. Since payment depends only on the second-highest bid (not my own bid, given I win), bidding exactly my value maximizes expected profit. With value $31, I will bid $31.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy since you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid. Overbidding risks negative profit if you win at a price above value, while underbidding only risks losing profitable opportunities. With value $24, bidding exactly $24 maximizes expected profit regardless of others' strategies.
